The lowest common ancestor of Pergolide and Eletriptan is an Organosulfur Compound, and both are classified as Agent Affecting Nervous System, indicating a shared biological role in neural function. This suggests that Pergolide may exert its effects on Htr1b through a pathway that involves Eletriptan, potentially through a downstream effect on the nervous system. The integration of these pathways highlights a possible mechanism by which Pergolide could interact with Htr1b, though the exact nature of this interaction remains to be elucidated.
